title: ‘X-Men’ Movie Casts Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Christopher Abbott as Prof. X, Adam Driver as Mr. Sinister and Maya Boyd as Storm
description:
The MCU’s X-Men team is taking shape.

	Marvel Studios exec Kevin Feige announced the inaugural members of the mutant team at D23 on Friday. The cas
body:
The MCU’s X-Men team is taking shape.

	Marvel Studios exec Kevin Feige announced the inaugural members of the mutant team at D23 on Friday. The cast includes Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, Kit Connor as Cyclops, Samara Weaving as Emma Frost, Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Christopher Abbott as Prof. X and Maya Boyd as Storm. Adam Driver will be playing the villainous Mr. Sinister.

	The X-Men haven’t assembled on screen since Fox’s 2019 film “Dark Phoenix,” which starred James McAvoy as Prof. Charles Xavier, Michael Fassbender as Magneto, Jennifer Lawrence as Mystique, Nicholas Hoult as Beast, Sophie Turner as Jean Grey, Tye Sheridan as Cyclops, Alexandra Shipp as Storm, Evan Peters as Quicksilver and Kodi Smit-McPhee as Nightcrawler. This younger cast of actors starred in several Fox prequel films, including “First Class,” “Days of Future Past” and “Apocalypse.” They took over from Fox’s original cast of “X-Men” trilogy stars, which included Patrick Stewart (Xavier), Ian McKellen (Magneto), James Marsden (Cyclops), Kelsey Grammer (Beast), Halle Berry (Storm), Alan Cumming (Nightcrawler), Famke Janssen (Jean Grey) and Rebecca Romijn (Mystique).
	

	Except for Berry and Janssen, those original “X-Men” cast members are reprising their roles in this year’s “Avengers: Doomsday,” where they’ll cross over with the MCU stars to battle Doctor Doom (Robert Downey Jr.) 


	Some of the past “X-Men” stars returned in Marvel’s blockbuster “Deadpool & Wolverine,” starring Ryan Reynolds and Hugh Jackman. Channing Tatum debuted as the mutant Gambit, who will also be returning for “Doomsday.” Fox’s X-Men franchise ended anticlimactically with the 2020 spinoff “New Mutants,” starring Anya Taylor-Joy, Charlie Heaton and Maisie Williams. Now, the team will return for the first time in years as an official part of the MCU.

schema.headline: ‘X-Men’ Movie Casts Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Christopher Abbott as Prof. X, Adam Driver as Mr. Sinister and Maya Boyd as Storm

title: Jon Favreau’s ‘Oswald the Lucky Rabbit’ Miniseries Sets February Release Date on Disney+
description:
Oswald the Lucky Rabbit, one of Disney’s earliest characters who predated Mickey Mouse, is back for the 21st century.

	At the D23 fan event in Anah
body:
Oswald the Lucky Rabbit, one of Disney’s earliest characters who predated Mickey Mouse, is back for the 21st century.

	At the D23 fan event in Anaheim on Friday, Disney revealed the first look at its live action combined with hand-drawn 2D animation series “Oswald the Lucky Rabbit” that’s being written, directed and executive produced by Jon Favreau. The series is coming to Disney+ as a three-part miniseries in February 2027.


	The cast includes Amy Sedaris, Kathryn Hahn, Steve Martin, Al Madrigal, Ravi Cabot-Conyers, Mykal-Michelle Harris and Ryder Allen. 
	

	Oswald was created by Walt Disney and Ub Iwerks in 1927 for Universal Pictures. The character proved to be a major milestone for Disney, as he and Iwerks created Mickey Mouse after Universal took control of Oswald in 1928. The Walt Disney Company reacquired the rights to the character in 2006, though it entered the public domain in 2023.

	Cabot-Conyers previously starred in Disney’s “Star Wars” series “Skeleton Crew,” which was executive produced by Favreau, and voiced one of the Madrigal family members in “Encanto.” Harris voiced Blaze in this summer’s “Toy Story 5” and previously starred in “Mixed-ish.” Sedaris and Favreau have collaborated already on “The Mandalorian” and “The Book of Boba Fett.” Meanwhile, Hahn is playing Mother Gothel in the live-action “Tangled” remake.

	Created just one year before Mickey Mouse, Oswald has attained cult status in Disney history. He’s largely vanished from pop culture and any of Disney’s titles, but he reappeared in the 2010 video game “Epic Mickey” — in which he and the famous mouse shared the screen for the first time. Oswald then made his first appearance in 85 years in the 2013 animated short “Get a Horse!”

schema.headline: Jon Favreau’s ‘Oswald the Lucky Rabbit’ Miniseries Sets February Release Date on Disney+

title: ‘VisionQuest’ Trailer: Paul Bettany and James Spader Return as Vision and Ultron in ‘WandaVision’ Trilogy Finale
description: Paul Bettany is back as Marvel‘s most popular android Vision in the upcoming Disney+ series, “VisionQuest.” The eight-episode series’ release date i
body:
Paul Bettany is back as Marvel‘s most popular android Vision in the upcoming Disney+ series, “VisionQuest.” The eight-episode series’ release date is set for Oct. 14.

	The show features Bettany’s first live-action MCU role since “WandaVision,” the inaugural Marvel TV show on Disney+ that starred him and Elizabeth Olson’s Wanda Maximoff/Scarlet Witch. Bettany began his Marvel journey way back in the first “Iron Man” movie as J.A.R.V.I.S., the AI voice that controls Tony Stark’s powerful suit of armor. He’s brought to life as the robot Vision in “Avengers: Age of Ultron,” where Bettany debuted the character and later joined the team along with Olson’s Wanda. However, Thanos kills Vision in “Avengers: Infinity War” by ripping the Mind Stone from his forehead, which throws Wanda into a depression over the death of her lover.
	

	In “WandaVision,” the former heroine takes over a New Jersey town and creates a fake, sitcom-inspired world where she and a magically-created, amnesiac Vision live happily ever after with their two kids, Tommy and Billy. Once Wanda’s ruse is uncovered, the real Vision (now sporting a white costume) is reanimated and has his full memory restored. He flies off, and Wanda later seemingly dies after going full villain in “Doctor Stranger in the Multiverse of Madness.”


	Now, Bettany’s Vision appears in both android and human form in “VisionQuest” alongside several of Marvel’s other famous AI robots. James Spader returns as Ultron, Emily Hampshire is E.D.I.T.H., Orla Brady is F.R.I.D.A.Y., James D’Arcy is J.A.R.V.I.S., T’nia Miller is Jocasta and Ruaridh Mollica is the grown-up version of Tommy Maximoff.
	

	See the trailer below.

schema.headline: ‘VisionQuest’ Trailer: Paul Bettany and James Spader Return as Vision and Ultron in ‘WandaVision’ Trilogy Finale

title: ‘Dead Souls’ Review: Alex Cox Betrays His Talent — Again — in His Latest Arid Didactic Western Doodle
description: “Dead Souls” is the new movie directed by Alex Cox, which means that for the umpteenth time over the last four decades, the director of “Sid and Nan
body:
“Dead Souls” is the new movie directed by Alex Cox, which means that for the umpteenth time over the last four decades, the director of “Sid and Nancy” and “Repo Man” has made a movie that almost no one will see or care about. Cox crowdfunded the film with a Kickstarter campaign, and it’s yet another of his arid didactic put-on Westerns. This one stars Cox himself as a mysterious and formidable old man in an undertaker’s suit and parson’s hat who wanders into an Arizona border town in 1890 to gather the names of dead Mexican laborers. “Dead Souls,” which is loosely based on the 1843 Nikolai Gogol novel of the same title, has kicked around at film festivals, and it premiered tonight at the Roxy Cinema, an off-the-beaten-track theater in New York. Is it a good movie? No, not really. But it’s one that inspires me to imagine — as every Alex Cox movie does — the glory of what might have been.  
	

	If I were asked to make a list of all the fantastic movie directors who never lived up to their promise, the No. 1 person on that list would be Alex Cox. This November, it will be 40 years since the release of “Sid and Nancy,” which I still think is one of the greatest movies ever made. It’s the greatest punk movie, the greatest music biopic, and a shattering and unexpectedly moving love story. The critic Terrence Rafferty described it as “‘A Hard Day’s Night’ in hell.” You could also call it “Romeo and Juliet” with knives and smack. It was Gary Oldman’s first film, and though he has never showed it much respect, I’m not kidding when I say that I think it’s still Oldman’s greatest performance — he brilliantly re-creates the sneering, self-mutilating, dumb-fuck surface of who Sid Vicious was, but he also gives him a teasing inner life that’s indelible. Chloe Webb’s performance as Nancy Spungen, the junkie girlfriend who Sid probably murdered (the role of Nancy was originally supposed to go to Courtney Love), is breathtaking in the nakedness of its emotion.
	

	Prior to “Sid and Nancy,” Alex Cox, a Britisher born in Merseyside, had made just one film, “Repo Man” (1984), that exquisite punk comedy of L.A. disaffection. It became an instant cult classic, with lines of dialogue that loomed like koans over the ’80s (“The more you drive, the less intelligent you are,” “Ordinary fucking people. I hate ’em”). But as inspired in its absurdist nihilism as “Repo Man” was, there’s no way that anyone connected with his follow-up film, including the movie’s producer Eric Fellner, could have anticipated the raw humanity that Alex Cox would bring to “Sid and Nancy.”

	The thing that always got me about “Sid and Nancy” — and I saw it probably 20 times in the ’80s — is that it was a total punk party, but in its rollicking way it was a work of classicism, made with a force of empathy that was undeniable. It wasn’t just hilarious; it was dead serious. It was true to the damaged wrecks Sid and Nancy were, yet it made them more complicated than you could have believed. The final scene, with Sid dancing with some kids around a boom box in a trash-strewn heaven, never failed to bring me to tears. Forget “Sex, Lies, and Videotape.” To me, the year that truly launched the independent-film revolution was 1986, the year of “Blue Velvet” and “Sid and Nancy.” I was dizzy with anticipation at what Alex Cox would do next.

	He proceeded — figuratively — to shoot himself in the foot, the thigh, the gut, and the head. He self-destructed. But he did it almost on purpose, by directing movies that were more or less unreleasable. The year after “Sid and Nancy,” Cox went to Spain to make a low-budget satirical spaghetti Western that he wrote in three days called “Straight to Hell.” It starred Joe Strummer and Courtney Love and featured a roster of hip musicians (Shane MacGowan, Elvis Costello, Grace Jones), and it was a scrappy kitsch travesty of a movie that never pretended to be more than a throwaway. I thought, “Okay fine, that was something Alex Cox had to get out of his system.” (Kind of like when Steven Soderbergh, a decade later, cleaned his pipes by making “Schizopolis.”)

	But later that same year, Cox released his big-budget studio follow-up, “Walker,” a historical Western about William Walker (played by Ed Harris), the American freebooter of the 1850s who led a mercenary army into the Nicaraguan civil war and wound up installing himself as the nation’s president. Western hubris? You bet, and Cox never let you forget it. The film was a left-wing Sunday-school lesson dressed up as…another tossed-together Cox neo-Western. “Walker” was a slovenly disaster. The film cost $6 million and grossed just $300,000. But it was a special kind of bomb. When “Sid and Nancy” was coming out, I interviewed Cox, talking to him in a Park Avenue hotel room, and while I liked him tremendously (he was funny, sharp, impassioned), I was struck by his unforgiving moralistic fervor, which he had already begun to aim like a howitzer at studio executives. He talked about them like they were the devil. When I saw “Walker” a year later, I put two and two together: The movie was an arch, sloppy, who-gives-a-fuck mess because Cox had made it that way deliberately. It was my feeling that on some level, consciously or unconsciously, his desire to fuck over the studio was so great that it led him to sabotage his own career.
	

	Cox was done as a mainstream filmmaker. He moved to Mexico and settled down there, and after a while you heard that he was still making films. I was eager to see “Highway Patrolman,” his 1991 Spanish-language crime drama that was made down there, and at a certain point it was given a run at Film Forum in New York. The movie was…okay. (Not better than that.) You could tell that Cox was trying. But he’d lost the extraordinary creative juice that powered “Sid and Nancy” and “Repo Man.” And in my estimation, he has never gotten it back. He’s 71 now, and he’s still making sloppy absurdist “punk” japes, as if this was some sort of statement.

	Tall, snarky, and hungry, with a wedge of stand-up hair, Cox, in the 1980s, styled himself as a provocateur; I recently saw a scrappy documentary on YouTube about the making of “Sid and Nancy,” and you could see what a hellion he was. But in “Dead Souls,” the fresh punk has become an aging specter. Cox still has that thick head of hair (now slicked back), as well as the prominent mole on his left cheek, but in “Dead Souls” he gives off a parched vibe as stately and wizened as that of William S. Burroughs. His character is named Strindler (we know that because he says it 100 times), and Cox gives him a voice of sinister politeness that evokes the John Huston of “Chinatown.” At first, as Strindler goes about his mission of gathering the names of the dead, we think he might be some sort of Mephistopheles figure, like Robert De Niro in “Angel Heart.” We wait to solve the mystery of what he’s after.

	Cox shot the film in Almería, Spain (the picturesque backdrop for hundreds of spaghetti Westerns), as well as parts of Arizona, and there’s an inviting spaciousness to it. Yet the indoor scenes are dingy. Cox, working like a shoestring Peckinpah, sets up Strindler against the crooks who run the border town — the corrupt mayor and sheriff and a wealthy rancher. Strindler doesn’t know how to ride a horse or fire a gun (which is funny), and he climbs into a wagon operated by Borracho (Zander Schloss), the Wavy Gravy derelict who becomes his Sancho Panza. They ride off to visit an assortment of locals, with Strindler gathering names at each place for his book of the dead and paying for them. The drama is semi-playful in a static way.
	

	But to what end? As we learn what Strindler is really up to (it’s no coincidence that his name rhymes with “swindler”), the film, like a one-man-band “There Will Be Blood,” becomes a lesson in cutthroat capitalism. How timely…and how tiresome. (We have the DSA for that, thank you.) The film starts as a mystery, but once that’s solved, the only real mystery is why Alex Cox tied his film career to a stone marked “retro Marxist Western punk pretension” and then threw that stone into the water and plunged down after it, sinking to the bottom.

	What do I think he should have done otherwise? I think he should have grown up and recognized that making movies, because it involves so much money, requires compromise, and that all of the supreme filmmakers (except for maybe Orson Welles) understood that. If Cox had taken a different turn, who knows what amazing movies he might have given us? For two films, at least, he was a true artist. After that, you might say he stuck to his guns. Like Sid Vicious, he did it his way. He burned out and faded away. But I like to imagine an alternate universe in which Alex Cox continued to be the great filmmaker he was put on earth to be.

schema.headline: ‘Dead Souls’ Review: Alex Cox Betrays His Talent — Again — in His Latest Arid Didactic Western Doodle

title: CBS News Chief Correspondent Matt Gutman Accused of Sexual Harassment by Former ABC Field Producer
description: Matt Gutman, CBS News’ chief correspondent, has been accused of sexual harassment in a wrongful-termination lawsuit filed by a former co-worker at A
body:
Matt Gutman, CBS News’ chief correspondent, has been accused of sexual harassment in a wrongful-termination lawsuit filed by a former co-worker at ABC News.

	Gutman was named in a lawsuit filed by Samira Said, who worked as a field producer for ABC News in its Los Angeles bureau from May 2021 until March 2025. She alleges in the lawsuit she was wrongfully terminated by ABC and that Gutman contributed to a hostile work environment by making “sexualized” comments to her.
	

	Variety has reached out to representatives for ABC and Gutman for comment.


	According to Said’s lawsuit, during her employment at ABC, she was “placed on a male-only team including on-air correspondent Matt Gutman” and two additional male crew members. 

	“While the team waited in a public queue during the assignment, Gutman initiated a discussion rating a female correspondent’s appearance and reducing her professional standing to a numerical score based on her physical attributes,” the lawsuit alleges. “The male crew joined in, continuing to assess the woman’s body and looks in Said’s presence. The men attempted to draw Said into the conversation by soliciting her views. Said declined and stated the conversation was inappropriate.”

	On another occasion, according to the lawsuit, during a press day for a film release, Said and Gutman “disagreed about whether the team should leave the work site. In front of multiple coworkers, Gutman responded by making a sexualized insinuation that Said must have an after-hours date in the city and that this is why she did not want to relocate. The remark, made audibly to others, demeaned Said and reduced her professional judgment to a sexualized stereotype.”
	

	According to Said’s complaint, after she had been assigned to cover events at the school shooting in Uvalde, Texas, she “experienced severe psychological symptoms.” Per the lawsuit, prior to that assignment, she had contracted COVID-19 and “was still experiencing symptoms from COVID-19” while in Uvalde.

	Said was granted medical leave from August 2022 through January 2023, as her “psychiatrist continued to certify the medical necessity of her leave on a recurring basis” to ABC and Disney. Per the lawsuit, around January 2023, Said’s psychiatrist had cleared her to return to work, “subject to reasonable accommodations designed to enable her to perform the essential functions of the position while protecting against re-exposure to trauma triggers.” However, she claims in the lawsuit, ABC denied her accommodation requests and that ABC News’ L.A. bureau chief David Herndon “made it clear that unless she returned without restrictions and with full-week availability, she would not be permitted to resume her role.”

	“Following her medical leave and accommodation requests, Plaintiff was subjected to materially adverse treatment than she had experienced at any time prior to engaging in protected activity,” Said alleged in the lawsuit. She said around March 2023, Said was “demoted” to weekend desk shifts.

	Said said she was terminated by ABC on March 5, 2025. Shortly prior to that, when Said was in the field covering “hazardous weather-related events,” she “sustained a workplace injury when heavy equipment struck her foot, resulting in a bone contusion,” according to the lawsuit. “Said reported the injury to her supervisors. A Disney physician evaluated Said and determined that her foot injury did not require her to take leave.”

	Said is seeking unspecified monetary damages in the lawsuit, filed Friday in Superior Court of the State of California for the County of Los Angeles, Central District. Among other things, her complaint alleges discrimination and hostile work environment harassment; retaliation for engaging in protected activity; failure to provide reasonable accommodation; breach of express oral contract not to terminate employment without good cause; intentional infliction of emotional distress. A copy of the lawsuit is available at this link.
	

	Gutman joined CBS News on Jan. 5, 2026. In addition to reporting for “CBS Mornings” and “CBS Evening News,” he serves as a lead correspondent for “48 Hours” and will contribute to future seasons of “60 Minutes.” He previously spent more than 15 years at ABC News, where he most recently served as chief national correspondent.

schema.headline: CBS News Chief Correspondent Matt Gutman Accused of Sexual Harassment by Former ABC Field Producer

title: ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Trailer: Robert Downey Jr. Faces Off Against Mister Fantastic, X-Men and Avengers With Army of Sentinels
description: Marvel Studios unveiled the second “Avengers: Doomsday” trailer on Friday during Disney’s D23 fan convention, further teasing the massive MCU team-u
body:
Marvel Studios unveiled the second “Avengers: Doomsday” trailer on Friday during Disney’s D23 fan convention, further teasing the massive MCU team-up movie arriving in theaters Dec. 18.

	The two-minute clip — introduced by “Doomsday” leads Robert Downey Jr. (Doctor Doom), Chris Evans (Steve Rogers/Captain America) and Hayley Atwell (Peggy Carter) — sees Vanessa Kirby’s Sue Storm warning a collection of Earth’s mightiest heroes about the danger of the Latverian villain in between cuts focused on Doom’s costume.
	

	“I knew he was lost,” Storm says. “But I did not realize that he was broken.” 


	The Avengers, Fantastic Four, Thunderbolts and more heroes are joining forces to take down Doctor Doom, the evil villain played by Robert Downey Jr. in his return to the MCU after his original Iron Man character died in “Endgame.”

	The cast is a sprawling who’s who of Marvel A-listers. In addition to Downey Jr. returning, Chris Evans is back as Steve Rogers/Captain America after he traveled back in time and stepped away from his superhero duties in “Endgame.” Chris Hemsworth also reprises his role as Thor, alongside Paul Rudd as Ant-Man, Letitia Wright as Black Panther, Sebastian Stan as the Winter Soldier, Tom Hiddleston as Loki and Simu Liu as Shang-Chi. 

	The “Fantastic Four: First Steps” stars, comprised of Pedro Pascal as Mister Fantastic, Vanessa Kirby as the Invisible Woman, Joseph Quinn as Human Torch and Ebon Moss-Bachrach as the Thing are back for “Doomsday,” as are the “Thunderbolts” cast, including Florence Pugh as Yelena Belova, David Harbour as Red Guardian, Lewis Pullman as Sentry, Wyatt Russell as U.S. Agent and Hannah John-Kamen as Ghost.
	

	Notably, “Doomsday” mark the official MCU debut for several of Fox’s past “X-Men” stars after Disney acquired the studio. Patrick Stewart is back as Prof. Charles Xavier, Ian McKellen is Magneto, James Marsden is Cyclops, Kelsey Grammer is Beast, Rebecca Romijn is Mystique, Alan Cumming is Nightcrawler and Channing Tatum is Gambit.

	Watch the trailer below:

title: ‘The Greatest Showman’ Stage Musical Sets Spring 2027 Opening at London’s Theatre Royal Drury Lane
description: Disney Theatrical Group’s stage adaptation of “The Greatest Showman” will open at Theatre Royal Drury Lane in London’s West End in Spring 2027, foll
body:
Disney Theatrical Group’s stage adaptation of “The Greatest Showman” will open at Theatre Royal Drury Lane in London’s West End in Spring 2027, following a sold-out run at the Bristol Hippodrome. 

	Oliver Tompsett and Samantha Barks will star as P.T. Barnum and Charity Barnum.

	The musical is based on the 2017 20th Century Studios film “The Greatest Showman,” with story by Jenny Bicks. It marks the first 20th Century Studios title, formerly 20th Century Fox, to be adapted for the stage by Disney Theatrical Group. The Seelig Group, a producer of the original film, is also producing the musical.
	

	The production features songs by Benj Pasek and Justin Paul, a book by Tim Federle and direction and choreography by Casey Nicholaw. The score includes “The Greatest Show,” “A Million Dreams,” “Come Alive,” “Rewrite the Stars,” “Never Enough” and the Golden Globe Award-winning “This Is Me,” alongside new songs written for the stage.


	Joining Tompsett and Barks in the company are Ben Joyce as Phillip Carlyle, Vajèn van den Bosch as Jenny Lind and Malinda Parris as Lettie Lutz. Further casting will be announced.

	“It’s rare for a new film musical to capture the world’s imagination in the way ‘The Greatest Showman’ has – both for its story and record-breaking soundtrack. The piece is fearless in its emotion: open-hearted, exuberant, and unapologetically joyous, celebrating those considered outsiders and dreamers,” said Anne Quart and Andrew Flatt of Disney Theatrical Group.

	Quart and Flatt said the production stems from a collaboration among Pasek and Paul, who return with the show’s established songs alongside new numbers written for the stage; Federle, whose book reflects a love of theatre; and two-time Tony Award winner Nicholaw, who directs a cast led by Tompsett and Barks.
	

	“We’re thrilled to begin this next chapter in our long association with Theatre Royal Drury Lane – this feels like a very special homecoming,” Quart and Flatt said.

	The musical continues Disney Theatrical Group’s longstanding relationship with LW Theatres’ Theatre Royal Drury Lane, which has hosted the company’s productions since the venue reopened following a restoration completed in 2021. Nicholaw’s production of “Hercules” is currently running at the venue.

	The creative team also includes Alex Lacamoire on music supervision and orchestrations, David Korins on scenic design, Gregg Barnes and Sky Switser on costume design, Natasha Katz on lighting design and Peter Hylenski on sound design.

	Disney Theatrical Group, led by Andrew Flatt and Anne Quart, has produced stage shows since its 1994 debut with “Beauty and the Beast,” earning 20 Tony Awards and more than 60 nominations across 10 Broadway titles. Disney Theatrical Group’s shows and experiences draw close to 40 million visitors each year in 300 cities across five continents.

	The new stage musical is separate from “Come Alive! The Greatest Showman Circus Spectacular,” a Disney-sanctioned circus production also inspired by the film, which is playing at the Empress Museum in Earls Court, London.

schema.headline: ‘The Greatest Showman’ Stage Musical Sets Spring 2027 Opening at London’s Theatre Royal Drury Lane

title: ‘Percy Jackson’ Season 3 Trailer: ‘The Titan’s Curse’ Comes to Life With Prophecies and a Quest to Save Annabeth
description:
Things are starting to heat up at Camp Half-Blood.

	Disney+ released the first trailer for Season 3 of “Percy Jackson and the Olympians,” which wil
body:
Things are starting to heat up at Camp Half-Blood.

	Disney+ released the first trailer for Season 3 of “Percy Jackson and the Olympians,” which will premiere Nov. 20. In the trailer, Percy grapples with a dream about The Great Prophecy. “Something bad is coming,” he says over voiceover.

	The official synopsis for Season 3 reads: “When Annabeth is captured by the forces of Kronos, Percy must embark on a perilous journey to rescue her. He must free a goddess in chains, confront the Titan’s curse, and avoid triggering the fall of Olympus. With Grover by his side, Percy must join some unlikely questmates to confront a prophecy with dire consequences.”
	

	The cast includes Walker Scobell as Percy Jackson, Aryan Simhadri as Grover Underwood, Leah Sava Jeffries as Annabeth Chase and Dafne Keen as the goddess Artemis. 


	Also returning for Season 3 are Charlie Bushnell as Luke Castellan, Daniel Diemer as Tyson and Dior Goodjohn as Clarisse La Rue. New Greek gods will also be introduced, including Hubert Smielecki as Apollo, Kate McKinnon as Aphrodite and Ming-Na Wen as Hera. 

	The show’s cast and crew stopped by San Diego Comic-Con in July to release the first few minutes of Season 3, which opened with Thalia Grace battling a monster. During the show’s panel, Scobell teased he believed this would be the most book-accurate adaptation they’ve done thus far. 

	“Percy Jackson and the Olympians” is based on Riordan’s bestselling book series of the same name, which was first released in 2005. The author created the Disney+ series with Jonathan E. Steinberg, who serves as the co-showrunner and executive producer alongside Craig Silverstein and Dan Shotz. Additional executive producers include Riordan and his wife, Rebecca; the Gotham Group’s Ellen Goldsmith-Vein, Jeremy Bell and D.J. Goldberg; Bert Salke; James Bobin; Jim Rower; Albert Kim; Jason Ensler; and Sarah Watson. 
	

	Watch the trailer below.

schema.headline: ‘Percy Jackson’ Season 3 Trailer: ‘The Titan’s Curse’ Comes to Life With Prophecies and a Quest to Save Annabeth

title: ‘The Bluey Movie’ First Look: Bluey and Her Family Hit the Big Screen With New 3D Animation Style
description: Disney and BBC Studios have released the first look at “The Bluey Movie,” marking the first time the animated children’s series will be adapted for
body:
Disney and BBC Studios have released the first look at “The Bluey Movie,” marking the first time the animated children’s series will be adapted for the big screen.

	Premiering in theaters Aug. 6, 2027, the film continues Bluey’s adventures with her Mum, Dad and little sister, Bingo. Melanie Zanetti will reprise her role as Bluey’s mom, Chilli, from the series, with Richard Jeffrey returning to voice Bluey’s dad, Bandit. 
	

	The biggest difference from the trailer and the show is a fresh 3D animation style, in which Bluey and Bingo play a game of “Keepy Uppy” with a balloon.


	Series creator Joe Brumm writes and directs the movie, with Richard Jeffrey (“Bluey” Seasons 1-3) co-directing. Amber Naismith (“The Lego Movie”) serves as producer, and Jeff Bush provides the score for the Ludo Studio production. Executive producers include Brumm, Charlie Aspinwall and Daley Pearson for Ludo Studio and Justine Flynn for BBC Studios. President of Disney Live Action and 20th Century Studios David Greenbaum will oversee the film for Disney. BBC Studios finances and licenses the film with theatrical distribution through Walt Disney Studios. 

	“Bluey” first premiered in 2018 and has since transformed into a global phenomenon, becoming the most watched series worldwide on Disney+ in 2024 and receiving an International Emmy Kids Award and BAFTA Children’s and Young People’s Award.

	Alan Bergman and Dana Walden, the co-chairs of Disney Entertainment, previously said the series has united “families everywhere with its heartfelt stories of play, imagination and connection. We are so proud to expand upon our relationship with BBC Studios to bring the magic of ‘Bluey’ to the big screen — for real life! — and we are deeply grateful to Joe Brumm for creating a world that continues to inspire and delight families everywhere.”
	

	See the teaser trailer and the first poster below.





	

									THE BLUEY MOVIE

schema.headline: ‘The Bluey Movie’ First Look: Bluey and Her Family Hit the Big Screen With New 3D Animation Style

title: ‘Tangled’ Sets March 2028 Release Date as First Footage Debuts at D23
description:
Disney has set a March 31, 2028 release date for its live-action adaptation of “Tangled.” 

	The news was revealed during the Disney Entertainment S
body:
Disney has set a March 31, 2028 release date for its live-action adaptation of “Tangled.” 

	The news was revealed during the Disney Entertainment Showcase at the D23 fan event in Anaheim Friday, where the first footage from the “Tangled” remake was shown exclusively to those in attendance.

	Starring Teagan Croft as Rapunzel and Milo Manheim as Flynn Rider, the film follows the same Brothers Grimm fairytale as the 2010 animated movie about the princess with magically long hair. After spending years locked away in an isolated tower, Rapunzel is eventually rescued by the fugitive thief, Flynn Rider. 
	

	The live-action cast includes Kathryn Hahn as Mother Gothel, the film’s antagonist who locks Rapunzel away, and Diego Luna playing a new role. Patrick and Hugo McPherson play the Stabbington brothers, two twin villains.


	“I love playing Mother Gothel. She’s stunning, hilarious, fab, kind, generous to a fault,” Hahn said from the D23 stage Friday. “Might be overprotective but that’s because she cares so much.”

	Michael Gracey, who previously helmed “The Greatest Showman,” directs the film from a screenplay by Jennifer Kaytin Robinson and Michael Montemayor. Lucy Kitada and Jessica Virtue executive produce, while Kristin Burr serves as producer.

	Filming began in Spain in June. The “Tangled” live-action remake was first reported to be in development in December 2024 but was put on hold the following April after the “Snow White” adaptation failed to impress at the box office, earning only $69 million domestically and $145 million globally.

	The original 2010 film brought in $592 million at the global box office, with Mandy Moore voicing the bubbly, long-haired princess and Zachary Levi voicing the arrogant Flynn. Its success has led to various spinoffs, including the short film “Tangled Ever After” and series “Rapunzel’s Tangled Adventure.” The movie’s hit song, “I See the Light,” earned an Oscar nomination for best original song at the 2011 ceremony, plus Golden Globe noms for best animated feature and song.

title: Luigi Mangione Sketch Artist Says He Finally Showed Emotion in Court While Pleading Guilty
description:
Luigi Mangione
                          Seemed to Grapple With Gravity of Crime in Court, Sketch
body:
Luigi Mangione
                          Seemed to Grapple With Gravity of Crime in Court, Sketch Artist Says
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 14, 2026
                            6:03 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Luigi Mangione seemed to finally feel the full weight of his crime in court, becoming emotional during the proceedings ... so says the sketch artist.
      
    
            Christine Cornell -- who has sketched Luigi numerous times during his legal journey -- said on CNN he's always seemed distant in the courtroom ... listening intently to the hearings but not conveying any feeling.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            She likens him to a husky ... a beautiful dog -- but it's impossible to tell exactly what they're thinking.
      

      
        
              
    
    
            However, she says today -- while admitting to killing UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson and pleading guilty to federal stalking charges -- she says he finally showed all of the emotion he'd seemingly been hiding.
      
    
            Christine says Luigi's voice shook and -- though he didn't cry -- he looked close to tears.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The CNN host Erin Burnett asks Christine if he could've been playing up the scene for the judge in order to possibly get a lighter sentence down the line ... but she shoots down the theory -- telling the host she's certain his emotions were genuine.
      
    
            As you know ... Luigi pled guilty to federal stalking charges -- without a deal with prosecutors in place. He's essentially throwing himself at the mercy of the court and hoping for a less severe sentence.
      
    
            Federal sentencing guidelines state Luigi should receive between 24 and 30 years ... and a judge has already stated he will need to serve 85% of his sentence. If given 24 years, Luigi could be out in 20.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            At least one of Brian Thompson's family members -- his uncle, Bruce Thompson -- told The Times he wants Luigi to "get what he deserves" adding the family wants the judge to hand out the maximum sentence possible.
      
    
            As for Luigi's state murder trial ... his lawyers have filed a documents arguing the guilty plea should mean double jeopardy is in play -- and that his New York state charges should be dismissed.

title: Nick Reiner Says He Never Gave Trustee Permission to Withhold Funds

Nick Reiner
                          I Never Told My Trustee Keep My Money
body:
Nick Reiner
                          I Never Told My Trustee Keep My Money
                      
                  
                                                                        Published

                                                                      |

                                  August 14, 2026
                                6:03 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Nick Reiner is calling BS on the executor of his trust ... telling the court he didn't give any consent to withhold money from him he says was owed to him under the terms of the trust when he turned 30.
      
    
            Reiner filed a new legal document on Friday in which he says successor trustee Jodi Pais Montgomery's claim that he told a past trustee he'd leave the money in the account as "trust property" isn't true.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            He also says the claim that his mother, Michele Reiner, told a previous trustee that he knew he could take the money when he turned 30 and therefore was consenting to leave it in the account when he didn't remove it is also not valid consent ... because he didn't authoritze his mother or anyone to make such a statement.
      

            Reiner says he wasn't told by anyone he could take the money from the account, and he wants his money along with the accrued interest he's owed.  He says the trustee has listed these amounts owed at age 30 at around $558K.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As you know ... Reiner needs the cash for his legal defense. He was recently indicted for the murder of his parents, Rob and Michele.
      
    
            He was briefly represented by attorney Alan Jackson ... who dropped his case when he couldn't pay his legal fees with the money in his trust.

title: 'Botched' Star Dr. Terry Dubrow Victim of Cyberattack, Patient Data Stolen
description:
'Botched' Star Dr. Terry Dubrow
                          Cybercriminals Got Their Hands on My Pa
body:
'Botched' Star Dr. Terry Dubrow
                          Cybercriminals Got Their Hands on My Patients' Data
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 14, 2026
                            5:00 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Dr. Terry Dubrow has a whole different kind of "Botched" situation on his hands ... cybercriminals breached his plastic surgery practice and accessed sensitive patient information.
      
    
            Terry tells TMZ ... cybercrooks have become so sophisticated with A.I. and other technology that "literally no business, big or small, is safe." He says he spent a tremendous amount of money and resources protecting his patients' data -- and stresses there's no evidence any of it has been misused or shared.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Terry's also trying to give patients some peace of mind ... telling us he has a $1 million cyber protection insurance policy for them and set up a free monitoring service going forward.
      

            According to a notice filed with the California Attorney General, the breach began in January 2025.
      
    
            Terry's practice confirmed last month that patient data was taken, and on Thursday they began notifying those affected.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            Depending on the patient, the data may include Social Security and driver's license numbers, addresses, birth dates, and prescription and treatment records ... along with procedure images and X-rays.
      
    
            The practice says the breach has been contained and reported to the FBI ... and affected patients are being offered complimentary identity protection.
      
    
            What a time to be alive.
